articles.title: 🧠 A.I. Reads Your Brain Scan In Seconds; Immediately Has Notes On Your Life Choices
articles.dateline: ANN ARBOR — reported at the speed of a synapse
paras: Researchers unveiled an AI system that can interpret a brain MRI in mere seconds, accurately flagging a wide range of neurological conditions — a genuinely impressive breakthrough only slightly undercut by how quickly it now knows more about your head than you do.

"It's remarkably accurate," a researcher said, of a system that read a scan, delivered a diagnosis, and then, entirely unprompted, suggested the patient "get more sleep and text their mother back." Doctors welcomed the speed, noting the machine finishes reading the scan before the printer has even warmed up.

articles.title: 🚪 Google Expands Its A.I. Empire, Loses The People Who Actually Built It; Empire Confused
articles.dateline: MOUNTAIN VIEW — reported from an increasingly empty desk
paras: Google is aggressively expanding its AI empire while simultaneously losing many of the researchers who built it — a strategy roughly equivalent to constructing a much bigger ship while the crew quietly rows away in the lifeboats.

"We're deeply committed to our talent," the company said, addressing a room that had grown noticeably roomier. Industry watchers note the great AI talent war has reached the stage where engineers are traded like sports stars, minus the trading cards and plus a genuinely staggering signing bonus.

articles.title: 🕳️ Experts Warn Of A Dangerous New Cyber Era; Many Companies Reassuringly Unaware They're In It
articles.dateline: THE INTERNET — reported from inside an unlocked back door
paras: Security researchers say a recent high-profile hack marks the start of a dangerous new AI-driven cyber era — a warning made only slightly more alarming by the fact that many affected firms reportedly do not yet know anything happened to them at all.

"Awareness is the first step," one expert sighed, describing companies currently enjoying a blissful, breached serenity. The new threat landscape is fast, automated, and polite enough to let itself out afterward, leaving behind the digital equivalent of a thank-you note.

articles.title: 🤖 Humanoid Robots Get Cheap Enough To Impulse-Buy; Checkout Line Now Includes A Coworker
articles.dateline: SHENZHEN-ISH — reported from a very affordable android
paras: Humanoid robots are tumbling in price, with new models now cheap enough that they've crossed the dangerous threshold from "industrial investment" to "thing you add to your cart at 2am."

"It walks, it lifts, it makes uncomfortable eye contact," a rep beamed of a device now priced somewhere between a nice couch and a used hatchback. Analysts warn the impulse-buy humanoid is the natural endpoint of a civilization that already owns four air fryers.

articles.title: 🔌 Your Electricity Bill Now Partly Belongs To A Data Center You'll Never Meet
articles.dateline: THE POWER GRID — filed by candlelight, ironically
paras: As AI data centers draw ever more power, households living near them are watching their electricity bills climb — meaning a slice of your monthly payment now quietly subsidizes a warehouse of humming computers thinking very hard about nothing you asked for.

"It's simply the cost of progress," a utility rep explained to a family reading by the light of a single, resentful bulb. Experts recommend making peace with your new neighbor, which never sleeps, never says hello, and runs the AC at a temperature it flatly refuses to discuss.

horoscopes.text: An A.I. will diagnose you correctly today and then overshare. Boundaries — even with machines.
You will be recruited today, possibly by three companies and one alarmingly persuasive robot.
Mercury enters the power grid. Dim the lights; a data center is having its main-character moment.

tech_tip: If your company hasn't noticed a breach, that is not the same as not having one. Check the back door. It's ajar. It's always ajar.
gadget_watch: Humanoid robots are now impulse-buy cheap — congratulations on your new coworker, who never blinks and never leaves. Meanwhile living near a data center now shows up on your power bill, so enjoy subsidizing a building that thinks for a living.
